title: Introducing Mintlify Base
summary: Mintlify Base is now in beta. It's a workspace where people and agents work from the same specs, runbooks, and onboarding pages, kept current as your work changes.
body_markdown:
Base is now in beta. It's a workspace where people and agents work from the same specs, runbooks, and onboarding pages, kept current as your work changes. We already run Mintlify's own internal knowledge on it. This post was written, edited, and rewritten using Base.


Base runs on the same platform that powers Mintlify Docs, built for internal knowledge. The same editor, agents, and MCP server that serve your customers and their agents now serve your team and its agents.


## Agents read your internal knowledge too


Agents already account for more than[three-quarters](https://www.mintlify.com/data) of the traffic to the docs we host. The agents your team uses read internal pages the same way, and they[act on whatever context they're given](https://www.mintlify.com/blog/context-for-agents) . When a runbook is out of date, the agent repeats the old answer with confidence, and someone on your team spends the afternoon cleaning it up.


Most internal sites were built for people reading pages, with AI search added later. Search can find a page, but it can't fix one that's wrong.


## What you can do in Base


Base organizes knowledge into **Personal** pages for drafts you can share when they're ready, a **Shared with me** view for pages teammates send you, and a **Teamspace** for company-wide knowledge organized by folders.


### Write with an agent in the editor


Start from an idea, and an agent helps you draft, develop, and refine the page. Teammates can contribute from the web editor, the CLI, or their IDE, or hand the work to[Mintlify Agent](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/agent) from the dashboard or Slack.


Teammates review pages with comments and suggestions. Just tag Mintlify Agent in a comment on a section, the same way you'd tag a teammate. The agent edits the page without you leaving the conversation.


Give the agent your style guide, review checklist, or page templates once as a[skill](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/editor/agent#skills) , and it follows them on every page. Teamspace is backed by Git, so every change has history, but edits merge automatically. Nobody has to open or review a pull request to update a page.


### Connect every agent through MCP


Base includes a built-in[MCP server](https://mintlify.com/docs/ai/model-context-protocol) , so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or your in-house agents all read from the same source of truth. Mintlify also ships an[Admin MCP](https://mcp.mintlify.com/) that gives those same agents write access: they can edit pages, restructure navigation, open pull requests, and manage settings.


Pages are stored as Markdown files in a filesystem, the format agents already know how to search and navigate. In a controlled experiment we ran with a large engineering team using Claude Code on monorepos, structured Markdown[used about half the tokens and made agents 64% more precise](https://www.mintlify.com/blog/structured-docs-coding-agents) .


### Turn dense text into shareable interactive pages


Base turns long pages into editable, interactive pages with graphics, tables, and filters your team can scan at a glance. Pages support React components, and Mintlify Agent can create visual elements for you, including images, videos, Mermaid diagrams, and visualizations. Share pages internally with your team or externally as read-only links.


### Coming soon: Page verification


Soon, Base will tell you which pages are still right. Mark a page as verified and set an expiration date, so it comes up for review again before it goes stale. If a page is wrong or out of date, mark it as outdated or not verified for a set period of time. Readers can see who last verified a page, so they know whether to trust it.

## Get started


Base is in beta, and any team can sign up. Parts of it will change as we build with early teams. To set up your Teamspace, connect agents, and invite your team, start with the[Base docs](https://www.mintlify.com/docs/base/index) .


For the bigger picture, Han wrote about[why we built Base](https://www.mintlify.com/blog/your-wiki-is-becoming-a-codebase) .


[Sign up for Base →](https://www.mintlify.com/base)
